cover letter
CA Driver’s License (Required)
High School Diploma or Equivalent (Required)
Experience using spreadsheets and/or databases.

The Field Technicians will support data collection focused on plant communities, arthropods, soil and root microbiomes, grass outplanting success, metabolomics, and wildlife monitoring across multiple field sites and controlled experiments, with training and oversight provided by project personnel. Work will involve extensive field sampling in remote environments, field data collection, greenhouse support, laboratory processing, arthropod specimen handling, and detailed data management following standardized scientific protocols.
Field Sampling at Research sites - 35%

Primary responsibilities include conducting vegetation surveys using CNPS Relevé quadrat sampling protocols; installing and maintaining wildlife monitoring equipment; ground-dwelling arthropod sampling and processing; assisting with soil, rhizosphere, and grass root endosphere sampling for microbiome analyses; and assistance with seedling propagation, outplanting, and monitoring of outplanting success.
Processing wildlife camera and sound recorder data - 20%

This position requires the ability to work safely and independently in remote field settings under variable weather and terrain conditions. Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and adherence to safety protocols are essential. The project offers experience in plant and insect ecology, developing familiarity with flora and fauna in the South Fork Eel watershed, biodiversity monitoring, and plant biology.
Assisting with educational and outreach events - 10%
Greenhouse plant care - 15%
Processing biological samples (arthropod, plant) - 20%
Familiarity with/willingness to learn about California native plant communities and common grassland species.
Understanding of/willingness to learn standard field sampling techniques for vegetation, arthropods, soils, and wildlife monitoring.
Familiarity with/willingness to learn about greenhouse plant propagation.
Ability to work in remote field settings.
Plant identification skills and/or willingness to learn regional flora.
Ability to hike over steep and uneven terrain while carrying field equipment and supplies.
Strong organizational and record-keeping skills, including maintaining detailed field notes and data collection.
Ability to work outdoors for extended periods under varying weather conditions.
Effective written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to maintain careful attention to detail during repetitive sampling and laboratory procedures.
Ability to maintain professional conduct and strong safety awareness during field and laboratory operations.
Ability to work flexible hours.
